notes: The metadata lock instrument (wait/lock/metadata/sql/mdl) is disabled (the MySQL 5.7 default), so metadata locks are not recorded. Enable it at startup with performance-schema-instrument='wait/lock/metadata/sql/mdl=ON' in my.cnf, or now with: UPDATE performance_schema.setup_instruments SET ENABLED='YES', TIMED='YES' WHERE NAME='wait/lock/metadata/sql/mdl'; (locks taken before that stay invisible). myflames only reads, so it never changes this setting.

MySQL 5.7 lists only the row locks involved in a wait (information_schema.INNODB_LOCKS). Locks that block nobody are not visible through SQL; rows locked and lock structs in the transactions table count them. MySQL 5.7 also shows record-only and next-key locks both as X, and gap and insert-intention locks both as X,GAP.

Rows a transaction inserted, and index entries its updates wrote, are protected by implicit locks, which InnoDB lists only after another session conflicts with them. A transaction can hold more locks than the list shows.

While a DDL statement such as ALTER TABLE waits for its exclusive metadata lock, new reads and writes of that table queue behind it, even when the lock the blocker holds (usually SHARED_READ or SHARED_WRITE from an open transaction) would let them through. One open transaction and one waiting DDL statement can stop every read and write of the table until the transaction ends or the DDL gives up after lock_wait_timeout (by default one year on MySQL, one day on MariaDB). Stopping the DDL statement (KILL QUERY on its connection) also releases the queue, but an ALTER TABLE stopped at its final step loses the work it has done and must run again.

Performance Schema is not recording metadata locks here (it is off, or the wait/lock/metadata/sql/mdl instrument is disabled; MySQL 5.7 disables the instrument by default), so myflames cannot see exactly which session holds the table a DDL statement waits for. The likely blockers are open transactions, idle ones and ones that started before the DDL first: a transaction keeps the metadata locks of every table it used until it commits or rolls back. An ALTER TABLE that adds a foreign key or renames the table also locks the parent tables, so the blocker may be using a related table. Transactions that used only non-InnoDB tables (MyISAM, MEMORY, Aria) hold metadata locks too but are not in INNODB_TRX, so they are missing from this list. For exact blockers, add performance_schema=ON and performance-schema-instrument='wait/lock/metadata/sql/mdl=ON' under [mysqld] in my.cnf and restart. myflames changes neither.

myflames ends a session only when you choose Kill blocker (or run myflames locks --kill ID) and confirm. KILL QUERY n stops only the running statement; inside a transaction (after START TRANSACTION or BEGIN, or with autocommit=0), the transaction stays open and keeps its row and metadata locks until it commits or rolls back (in autocommit mode the statement is the whole transaction). KILL n closes the connection and rolls back its open transaction, which can take a while after many changes; its locks stay until the rollback ends. A prepared XA transaction survives both; end it with XA COMMIT or XA ROLLBACK.
Each section comes from a separate query, so a lock can appear or disappear between sections.
